attacks.claim: `.day-card` hardcodes a white background while its text uses `var(--text)`, which becomes near-white under dark mode. Titles, day headings, and muted meta text become near-invisible for the ~30% of users on dark mode, and the QA covered light mode only.
attacks.evidence: .day-card { background: #ffffff; color: var(--text); ... } with @media (prefers-color-scheme: dark) { :root { --text: #f2f2f7; --muted: #a1a1a6; --surface: #1c1c1e; } }; QA: "Chrome 1440px (light), Safari iPhone 14 (light) — pass"

attacks.claim: The 72px fixed mobile action bar has no matching bottom padding or spacer on `.planner` or `body`, so Sunday's day card and its tiles can sit under the bar and be unreachable. No iOS safe-area handling is described either.
attacks.evidence: .action-bar { position: fixed; ... height: 72px; } with .planner { ... padding: 16px; ... } and no bottom offset; "Sunday is the last child of .planner"

attacks.claim: Tile images have `width="320"` with no CSS `max-width` or responsive rule. Inside a 360px viewport the card content box is about 296px, so the image can overflow and break the tile layout on the smallest mobile width.
attacks.evidence: ; ABSENT: any img rule in planner.css

attacks.claim: Removing the one-tap "+ List" control makes the most frequent planner action (9.4 adds/week per WAU, 64% on mobile) a multi-screen path. The artifact provides no offsetting shortcut and does not justify the trade-off against its own usage data.
attacks.evidence: "The old tile-level "+ List" button is removed to declutter tiles." vs. "tap the tile → recipe page → "Ingredients" tab → choose servings in the servings sheet → "Add to list" → toast with "Undo""

attacks.claim: Recipe tiles have no link or button that opens the recipe page. The title is a plain h3 and the only controls are Swap and the overflow menu, so keyboard users cannot reach the "tap the tile" flow that the add-to-list path depends on.
attacks.evidence:
• Sheet-pan gnocchi

    ... ... (no anchor or handler wraps the tile)

attacks.claim: The spec does not define what happens when a drag or "Move to…" targets a day or slot that is already occupied. With a 3-tile cap this can yield 4 tiles or overwritten recipes, and the tile markup has no slot identifier for addressing breakfast/lunch/dinner.
attacks.evidence: "Each day is a `.day-card` with up to 3 recipe tiles (breakfast/lunch/dinner)." / "Drag a recipe tile between days to move it." / <li class="tile"> has no slot attribute; ABSENT: collision and slot-targeting behavior

attacks.claim: "Generate shopping list" writes all planned recipes' ingredients in one tap with no confirmation, preview, bulk undo, dedupe, or partial-failure behavior. Undo is specified only for single adds, and the bulk action and "Share plan" have no QA or prototype evidence.
attacks.evidence: "New sticky bottom bar on mobile with "Generate shopping list" (adds all planned recipes for the week) and "Share plan""; "toast with 'Undo'" appears only in the single-recipe flow; QA lists only "Shopping list add via recipe page + undo: pass"

attacks.claim: Failure paths for the new write actions are unspecified: add-to-list API errors or timeouts, drag-move persistence failure, and bulk-generate partial failure. The QA covers only success paths, so a failed write could show success or silently lose the user's change.
attacks.evidence: QA: "Shopping list add via recipe page + undo: pass." and "Drag-and-drop between days … pass."; ABSENT: error, offline, or partial-failure cases

attacks.claim: "Share plan" exports a user's weekly meal and schedule data outside the app, but the artifact does not say what the shared payload contains, whether the link is public or unguessable, whether it expires, or whether the user is told before sharing.
attacks.evidence: <button class="btn-ghost">Share plan</button>; ABSENT: description of transmitted data, link visibility or expiry, or consent

attacks.claim: QA does not cover the mobile path that carries 68% of sessions: no 360px capture, no touch drag-and-drop results, no Android, and no dark mode. Visual QA is light-mode desktop and iPhone 14 only, so the defects above could not have been caught.
attacks.evidence: "Visual QA vs Figma: Chrome 1440px (light), Safari iPhone 14 (light) — pass"; "Drag-and-drop … with keyboard … and VoiceOver: pass"; ABSENT: touch-drag, 360px, Android, or dark-mode results

attacks.claim: The rollout moves to 100% of web users at once with no staged ramp or abort thresholds, even though the flag allows a gradual step. A regression in the new planner reaches every user before any signal is acted on.
attacks.evidence: "Ship to 100% Tue 10:00 PT behind `planner_v7`"; "Watch: planner page JS errors, shopping-list additions/WAU, planner bounce rate." (no thresholds or ramp stages)

attacks.claim: The watch signals have no numeric thresholds, owners, or rollback trigger. Nothing states at what level of JS errors, bounce rate, or add-to-list drop the flag gets flipped off, so the watch window cannot drive a decision.
attacks.evidence: "Watch: planner page JS errors, shopping-list additions/WAU, planner bounce rate."

attacks.claim: The watch list has no funnel or step metrics for swap, drag-move, bulk generate, or the longer recipe-page add flow, so a failure or abandonment in the new path would be invisible. There is also no holdout or control cohort, so post-launch comparisons are confounded.
attacks.evidence: "Watch: planner page JS errors, shopping-list additions/WAU, planner bounce rate."; "Ship to 100% Tue 10:00 PT" (no holdout specified)

attacks.claim: Multiple identical "Swap" buttons have no recipe-specific accessible name, so screen-reader users in a button list cannot tell which recipe each affects. The overflow button already uses the correct pattern.
attacks.evidence: <button class="btn-ghost">Swap</button> (no aria-label, repeated per tile); compare <button class="btn-icon" aria-label="More options for Sheet-pan gnocchi">

attacks.claim: The Undo toast has no specified live-region behavior, and the artifact gives no visible focus style or reduced-motion handling for the new drag and card interactions.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: aria-live or role="status" for "toast with 'Undo'"; ABSENT: :focus-visible rule and prefers-reduced-motion query in planner.css

attacks.claim: At 360px the two action-bar buttons share about 316px with a 12px gap. "Generate shopping list" and "Share plan" may wrap or clip inside the fixed 72px height, and no width rule for the bar buttons is shown.
attacks.evidence: .action-bar { ... height: 72px; padding: 12px 16px; display: flex; gap: 12px; } with .btn-primary { min-height: 48px; }; ABSENT: 360px capture or overflow rule

attacks.claim: "Generate shopping list" does not say whether already-listed ingredients are deduplicated, which servings are used, or what happens for an empty week.
attacks.evidence: "adds all planned recipes for the week"; ABSENT: dedupe, servings, and empty-week behavior

attacks.claim: The bulk generate action may fan out one add call per recipe (up to 21 tiles per week), and the artifact does not state whether it is batched or capped. Request count and latency would grow with plan size.
attacks.evidence: "New sticky bottom bar on mobile with "Generate shopping list" (adds all planned recipes for the week)"; ABSENT: endpoint, batching, or cap

attacks.claim: Rollback depends on flipping `planner_v7` off, but the artifact does not state where the flag is evaluated, how long a flip takes to reach cached clients, or whether the new writes (moves, bulk adds) use the existing schema the old planner can read.
attacks.evidence: "old planner remains available by flipping the flag off (same API, no data migration)"; ABSENT: flag evaluation point, propagation time, or schema compatibility statement

attacks.claim: The rollout watches per-user metrics (additions per WAU, bounce rate) without stating whether the telemetry is new, which identifiers it is tied to, or its retention.
attacks.evidence: "Watch: planner page JS errors, shopping-list additions/WAU, planner bounce rate."

attacks.claim: The release bundles day-card redesign, bottom bar, drag-and-drop, shopping-list flow change, and lazy-loading images behind one flag, which makes it harder to isolate a regression to one change.
attacks.evidence: "Ship to 100% Tue 10:00 PT behind `planner_v7`" alongside the listed changes

attacks.claim: Two add-to-list paths (per-recipe and bulk) are specified with no shared logic, which invites divergent handling of servings, dedupe, and undo.
attacks.evidence: "Generate shopping list" and "Add to list" → toast with "Undo", with no shared service mentioned
